- Personal laptops are prohibited except for a five-business-day IT continuity exception when a managed laptop is being repaired or replaced and the employee has no working device [documents/policies/equipment_policy.md].

If you need a personal laptop for work, you must get prior approval from IT and have it logged [documents/policies/equipment_policy.md].

result.title: Equipment Policy
result.text: # Equipment Policy Owner: IT Effective date: 2026-06-01 ## Purpose This policy defines what hardware NovaOps provides by role and work arrangement, and the rules for personal equipment. ## Standard issue - Full-time employees receive a managed laptop. - Contractors normally use registered BYOD (their own device, enrolled in NovaOps's device management so it meets the same baseline security requirements as a managed laptop). - Remote or hybrid employees with an approved addendum may receive a monitor and dock, in addition to their laptop. - Customer Success Managers may receive a headset, given how much of their work is calls. ## Personal laptops Personal laptops are not allowed for employees, with one narrow exception: a five-business-day IT continuity exception when a managed laptop is being repaired or replaced and the employee has no working device. IT must approve and log the exception before the employee uses a personal machine, even for those five days. ## Care and return Equipment remains NovaOps property. Employees are expected to take reasonable care of it — a lost charger is a shrug, a laptop left unlocked in a coffee shop is not. Accidental damage during normal use is covered by IT at no cost to the employee; loss or damage from clear negligence (e.g., leaving a laptop visibly unattended in an unlocked car) may be charged back at IT's discretion, case by case. All equipment must be returned through IT at offboarding or role change, per the Offboarding Policy — it is not something a departing employee keeps or a manager signs off on informally.

result.title: Acceptable Use Policy
result.text: # Acceptable Use Policy Owner: IT Effective date: 2026-06-01 ## Purpose NovaOps systems, accounts, and devices are provided for company work. This policy defines what counts as acceptable use and what employees and contractors must not do with company systems, regardless of whether they are on a managed device or a registered BYOD machine. ## Prohibited storage Do not store source code, customer data, or employment records in personal accounts of any kind — personal email, personal cloud drives, or personal note-taking apps. This applies even for short-term or "just this once" convenience, since a personal account is outside NovaOps's access controls and audit logging. ## External sharing External sharing of company data must go through approved systems and follow least privilege — share only what the recipient needs, for only as long as they need it. Personal cloud-sync tools (Dropbox, personal Google Drive, personal OneDrive, etc.) are not allowed for company files under any circumstance, including drafts. ## Enforcement A first violation typically results in a written warning and mandatory retraining; repeated or deliberate violations (e.g., knowingly exfiltrating customer data) are handled as a security incident and escalated to IT Security and HR together. When in doubt about whether a tool or a sharing method is approved, ask IT before using it — not after.

result.title: Remote Work Policy
result.text: # Remote Work Policy Owner: HR Effective date: 2026-06-01 ## Work model NovaOps is remote-first with hybrid hubs for teams and roles that benefit from regular in-person time. Remote employees may request a monitor and dock. Hybrid employees may request the same bundle, but only with an approved addendum on file — the addendum is what distinguishes an occasional hybrid visitor from someone provisioned for a hub desk. ## Working securely from home Working remotely does not relax NovaOps's security requirements — it just moves where they apply. Remote employees must use MFA (per the Security and MFA Policy) on every login, keep their home Wi-Fi on WPA2/WPA3 with a non-default password, and avoid working on customer or source-code data over public Wi-Fi without the company VPN. A managed laptop's disk encryption and screen lock are not optional to disable for convenience. ## Location changes Location changes must be reported to HR before payroll, benefits, tax, or equipment decisions are made — a move across state or country lines can change withholding, benefits eligibility, and even which equipment vendor can ship there, so HR needs advance notice rather than finding out after the fact.

result.title: Offboarding Policy
result.text: # Offboarding Policy Owner: HR and IT Effective date: 2026-06-01 ## Ownership split HR owns employment status (the official last working day and separation type), IT owns account suspension and device return, and managers own handoff notes (what the departing employee was working on, and who picks it up). Each party acts on its own piece without waiting for the others to finish theirs. ## Removal timing Highly restricted systems — BambooHR, AWS, Okta admin, GitHub admin, and payroll tools — must be removed on the last working day, or immediately for urgent separations (e.g., involuntary terminations, security-related departures). "Last working day" means access is cut at end of that day, not sometime during the following week. ## Equipment return The employee's managed laptop, and any additional equipment issued under the Equipment Policy (monitor, dock, headset), must be returned to IT within 5 business days of the last working day. For remote employees, IT arranges a prepaid return shipment rather than leaving equipment return to the employee's own expense. ## Knowledge transfer The manager's handoff notes should cover in-flight work, any credentials or accounts that only the departing employee knew about, and open commitments to customers or vendors. Handoff notes go in the team's shared documentation, not in a private message that leaves with the employee's account.

Preboarding starts when the signed offer or contractor agreement is complete. By about five business days before your start date, People Operations should have your legal name, preferred name, work location, employment type, and manager. By about three business days before your start date, IT should have the manager-approved access list and shipping address. If your laptop shipment, Okta invite, or calendar invitation is late, tell your manager and file the IT ticket. Your manager owns your onboarding plan. For example, Maya Cohen, a Customer Success Manager joining in Israel, is assigned a manager in Customer Success, a buddy, a Salesforce training path, and a first-month customer-shadowing schedule before day one. A Backend Engineer such as Daniel Levi should have Jira, GitHub, Slack, approved AWS read-only access, and a first issue or code-reading assignment. A Product Manager should have Jira, Figma, Miro, Slack, and customer notes ready. Use full names and NovaOps email addresses in onboarding requests. visible so it doesn't get silently dropped.

# SaaS Procurement Policy

Owner: Finance
Effective date: 2026-06-01

## Approval threshold

Older threshold: SaaS expansions above USD 5,000 require Finance approval. This is
superseded for Q3 2026 by the SaaS renewal freeze memo, which sets the threshold at
USD 7,500. Where the two disagree, the more recent memo governs.

## Before approving an expansion

Before approving a SaaS expansion (new seats, a new tier, or a new vendor), check:

- Contract term — does the current term even allow expansion mid-cycle?
- Seat usage — are existing seats near capacity, or is there room already?
- Renewal date — is a renewal coming up soon enough to fold this into that review?
- Owner department — who requested it and who is accountable for the spend?
- Security review — has this vendor cleared NovaOps's security requirements for
  the data it will touch?

## Process

Requests start with the owning department describing the business need, then go to
Finance for the threshold check above. Finance may loop in Security or IT
depending on what the vendor touches — that routing decision is Finance's call, not
the requester's.

## Seat-limited software

Some software (Webex is a recurring example) can hit its seat cap even when the
department is technically eligible under this policy. In that case the request is
not a procurement decision anymore — it is a capacity issue that IT tracks
separately until seats are reclaimed or an expansion is approved.

result.content:
# SaaS Procurement Policy

Owner: Finance
Effective date: 2026-06-01

## Approval threshold

Older threshold: SaaS expansions above USD 5,000 require Finance approval. This is
superseded for Q3 2026 by the SaaS renewal freeze memo, which sets the threshold at
USD 7,500. Where the two disagree, the more recent memo governs.

## Before approving an expansion

Before approving a SaaS expansion (new seats, a new tier, or a new vendor), check:

- Contract term — does the current term even allow expansion mid-cycle?
- Seat usage — are existing seats near capacity, or is there room already?
- Renewal date — is a renewal coming up soon enough to fold this into that review?
- Owner department — who requested it and who is accountable for the spend?
- Security review — has this vendor cleared NovaOps's security requirements for
  the data it will touch?

## Process

Requests start with the owning department describing the business need, then go to
Finance for the threshold check above. Finance may loop in Security or IT
depending on what the vendor touches — that routing decision is Finance's call, not
the requester's.

## Seat-limited software

Some software (Webex is a recurring example) can hit its seat cap even when the
department is technically eligible under this policy. In that case the request is
not a procurement decision anymore — it is a capacity issue that IT tracks
separately until seats are reclaimed or an expansion is approved.

Owner: Finance
Effective date: 2026-06-01

## Approval threshold

Older threshold: SaaS expansions above USD 5,000 require Finance approval. This is
superseded for Q3 2026 by the SaaS renewal freeze memo, which sets the threshold at
USD 7,500. Where the two disagree, the more recent memo governs.

## Before approving an expansion

Before approving a SaaS expansion (new seats, a new tier, or a new vendor), check:

- Contract term — does the current term even allow expansion mid-cycle?
- Seat usage — are existing seats near capacity, or is there room already?
- Renewal date — is a renewal coming up soon enough to fold this into that review?
- Owner department — who requested it and who is accountable for the spend?
- Security review — has this vendor cleared NovaOps's security requirements for
  the data it will touch?

Requests start with the owning department describing the business need, then go to
Finance for the threshold check above. Finance may loop in Security or IT
depending on what the vendor touches — that routing decision is Finance's call, not
the requester's.

## Seat-limited software

Some software (Webex is a recurring example) can hit its seat cap even when the
department is technically eligible under this policy. In that case the request is
not a procurement decision anymore — it is a capacity issue that IT tracks
separately until seats are reclaimed or an expansion is approved.

You generally cannot use a personal laptop for work at NovaOps [documents/policies/equipment_policy.md]. The policy states that personal laptops are not allowed for employees, except in a very narrow case: a five-business-day IT continuity exception when a managed laptop is being repaired or replaced and the employee has no working device [documents/policies/equipment_policy.md]. Even then, IT must approve and log the exception before the employee uses a personal machine [documents/policies/equipment_policy.md].

Most full-time employees receive a company-owned laptop, and contractors normally use registered BYOD (their own device, enrolled in NovaOps's device management) [documents/policies/equipment_policy.md]. Remote or hybrid employees with an approved addendum may receive additional equipment like a monitor and dock [documents/policies/equipment_policy.md].

If you need to use a personal device for any work-related purpose, you should first check with IT to see if an exception can be granted [documents/policies/equipment_policy.md]. They will likely require the device to be enrolled in NovaOps's device management to meet security requirements [documents/policies/equipment_policy.md]. 

In summary, the standard practice is to use the company-provided laptop for work, and personal laptops are only permitted under very specific, IT-approved circumstances [documents/policies/equipment_policy.md].

This policy defines what counts as acceptable use and what employees and contractors must not do with company systems, regardless of whether they are on a managed device or a registered BYOD machine. ## Prohibited storage Do not store source code, customer data, or employment records in personal accounts of any kind — personal email, personal cloud drives, or personal note-taking apps. This applies even for short-term or "just this once" convenience, since a personal account is outside NovaOps's access controls and audit logging. ## External sharing External sharing of company data must go through approved systems and follow least privilege — share only what the recipient needs, for only as long as they need it. Personal cloud-sync tools (Dropbox, personal Google Drive, personal OneDrive, etc.) are not allowed for company files under any circumstance, including drafts. ## Enforcement A first violation typically results in a written warning and mandatory retraining; repeated or deliberate violations (e.g., knowingly exfiltrating customer data) are handled as a security incident and escalated to IT Security and HR together. When in doubt about whether a tool or a sharing method is approved, ask IT before using it — not after.

# Onboarding Policy

Owner: HR
Effective date: 2026-06-01

## Who does what

HR creates the employee's profile, employment packet, and onboarding checklist. IT
creates Okta, the device record, and baseline access — but only after the offer is
signed, never before. Provisioning ahead of a signed offer is not permitted, even to
save time for a fast-moving start date.

## Role-based baseline access

Baseline access varies by role. Customer Success Managers specifically need Okta,
Slack, Notion, Salesforce, Webex, BambooHR employee self-service, and SupportDesk
viewer — this is the standard bundle for that role, not something each manager
requests individually.

## Checklist discipline

Do not mark onboarding tasks complete unless the system of record (the onboarding
database) says complete. A task that looks done from a Slack message or a verbal
confirmation is not the same as a task marked complete in the checklist — the
checklist is the source of truth that other teams rely on.

## Blocked access stays blocked

If Webex access is blocked by a seat issue, it should remain marked blocked in the
checklist until the seat issue is actually resolved — do not mark it complete as a
courtesy or because the rest of onboarding finished on time. A blocked item stays
visible so it doesn't get silently dropped.
